dialogue.text: The first morning of the new school term -- and Aoi is already running late.
No, no, no -- not on the very first day!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: fear

dialogue.text: Aoi skids to a stop at the station gate, one shoe half-laced and her bag hanging open.
Why today of all days? My alarm worked! I know it did!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: She digs through her pocket for her transit card — and freezes.
Wait. Where's my pass?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: fear

dialogue.text: Her face drains, then snaps back into motion. She drops to a crouch and checks every pocket with frantic speed.
Come on, come on, don't do this to me!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: fear

dialogue.text: Nothing. Then she remembers the folded slip of paper that had been tucked into her mailbox before dawn.
Seriously... I stopped to read that creepy note, and now my pass is gone?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anger

dialogue.text: The note had contained only one line: Check platform three before first bell.
A station attendant notices her panic and steps closer.
Are you all right, miss?
dialogue.speaker: Attendant

dialogue.text: I'm late, I'm cardless, and I'm trying very hard not to become a tragedy in a school uniform.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: fear

dialogue.text: If you lost a pass, check the bench by platform three. Someone turned one in.
dialogue.speaker: Attendant

dialogue.text: Aoi blinks. For one beat, the whole station feels too quiet.
Platform three... you're kidding.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: She bolts down the stairs, ponytail flying, weaving through commuters with breathless apologies.
Sorry! Excuse me! First-day emergency!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: At the far end of platform three sits a single student in a dark coat, though the morning is warm. Beside them: Aoi's transit pass.
Oh, thank goodness! That's mine—
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: happiness

dialogue.text: The student places a hand over the pass before she can grab it. Their expression is calm, unreadable.
Aoi Takamori. Class 1-B. Seat by the window.
dialogue.speaker: Stranger

dialogue.text: She stops so hard her bag swings into her hip.
...How do you know my name?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: If you take the overpass today, don't look down when the bell rings.
dialogue.speaker: Stranger

dialogue.text: Okay, wow. That's not a normal sentence.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: The stranger slides the pass toward her. Under it is a small brass token stamped with a crescent moon and the number 3.
Did my friends put you up to this? Because this prank is way too elaborate for eight in the morning.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: Keep that. You'll need it when you hear your name a second time.
dialogue.speaker: Stranger

dialogue.text: That made it worse. You know that, right?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anger

dialogue.text: A train roars through the station between them, wind whipping her blazer and stealing the heat from her face.
She shields her eyes. When the train passes, the bench is empty.
Nope. No. Absolutely not.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: fear

dialogue.text: Only her pass and the brass token remain on the seat.
People do not just vanish before homeroom!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anger

dialogue.text: Her heart hammers somewhere between fear and outrage. Then the station clock clicks forward.
Aah— school! Mystery later, attendance first!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: happiness

dialogue.text: She snatches up both items and runs, but at the top of the stairs she slows just enough to look at the token in her palm.
Seat by the window, huh... If that's true, who were you?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: surprise

dialogue.text: Clutching the strange brass moon, Aoi rushes toward the first day of term with a new knot of suspense under her ribs.
